newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end slightly higher.

text.p: Swiss shares ended an uneventful session marginally higher, buoyed by major pharmaceuticals.
Volumes were moderate with investors probably already concentrating on Friday's U.S. jobs data, one dealer said.

He said the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) may show a further rise if the resistance level around 3,730/735 points is overcome in the next few days. "But if not, the market might fall as far as 3,650 points", he added.
The SMI ended 1.1 points higher at 3,737.5 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index gained 0.8 points to end at 2,394.75.
Major pharmaceuticals Roche, Ciba and Sandoz were sought by U.S. and U.K. investors. Their share prices edged up by between 0.16 percent and 0.6 percent.
"The big three drew the whole market up", a dealer noted, adding the pharmaceuticals seemed to be the most attractive Swiss stocks for foreigners at the moment.
Roche was buoyed by a buy recommendation from Barclays, he also said.
Roche gained 15 francs to 9,250. Ciba and Sandoz, which plan to merge to form Novartis, hit new year highs at 1,610 and 1,515 francs, respectively.
Among banks, SBC rose 1.15 percent to 242 on low volume.
Food group Nestle was down eight francs to 1,390.
Insurer Winterthur ended 11 francs lower at 763 after announcing a first-half group net profit of 248.4 million francs, which was at the lower end of expectations.
The company predicted a double-digit 1996 profit increase and said it expected to pay a higher dividend.
